posts.title: Your Logs Shouldn't Store Secrets
bullets: Mask or remove access tokens, session identifiers and passwords before writing logs.
Review database connection strings, encryption keys and sensitive personal data.
Test logging paths in CI and production; restrict who can read the logs.
posts.takeaway: Keep useful audit trails without exposing credentials.
posts.caption: Logs should help investigate incidents—not expose credentials. Remove or mask access tokens, session IDs, passwords and connection strings before logging. Restrict access to logs and test for accidental leakage in CI and production. #AppSec #SecurityLogging #DevSecOps #CyberSecurity Save this for later.
